scope.description: Five restart-only cases over the real hashicorp/raft single-voter node (in-memory transport, real commit-tracking log store): produce a committed log with the actual leader, stop the node, then call NewRaft again over the unchanged stores with a fresh transport on the same address, and record whether NewRaft returns. Cases vary only the size of the committed-but-unapplied startup replay window (applies before the restart, plus an optional manual snapshot before shutdown) and MaxAppendEntries.
assumptions: RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore, which is the documented opt-in configuration for this feature.

Automatic snapshotting is disabled (SnapshotThreshold=math.MaxUint64, SnapshotInterval=1h) so the replay window is set explicitly instead of by timer; this models a node whose newest snapshot lags its commit index, which the default 120s SnapshotInterval plus 8192 SnapshotThreshold also produce at higher write rates.
Restarted instances are constructed with a null logger so that no logging occurs after the test completes; logging is not part of the observed mechanism.
The bounded 5s wait is not the evidence: a returning restart is expected to be ~ms, and the blocked case is additionally recorded as a goroutine stack in the startup replay path.
excluded: Multi-voter clusters, network faults, and on-disk (bolt) log stores are excluded; the mechanism observed is in the startup replay path, not in replication.
The FSM's own semantics are excluded: MockFSM only records applied logs, and no FSM behavior is asserted.

parameters.recorded_operands: persisted_commit_index, last_log_index, snapshot_index, last_applied_before_restart, replay_window, fsm_bound_entries_in_window (entry-type census using the prepareLog rule), max_append_entries, fsm_mutate_ch_capacity (read from the running instance), estimated_replay_batches, restart_returned, restart_elapsed_ms, restart_error, restart_stack_frames

basis.prefix: Each case builds one real single-voter cluster with opts{Peers:1, Bootstrap:true, CommitTrackingLogs:true} so the log store, stable store, snapshot store and FSM are produced by the target itself: the leader dispatches and commits the applied commands through the normal leaderLoop/dispatchLogs path, which stages the commit index via StageCommitIndex and stores the entries. Before shutdown the harness reads the store's persisted commit index, the last log index, cap(fsmMutateCh), the configured MaxAppendEntries, and censuses the entry types in the replay window with GetLog using the same rule as Raft.prepareLog. For the snapshot case it takes a user snapshot before shutdown and uses that snapshot's index as the restart's last-applied point. It then calls leader.Shutdown(), creates a fresh NewInmemTransport on the same address, and calls NewRaft over the unchanged logs/stable/snapshots instances as the target's own restart tests do, in a goroutine that reports completion through a channel; the harness waits up to 5s and, if nothing arrived, samples all goroutine stacks and keeps the one on the startup replay path. No production code is modified; the harness only reads state and drives the exported lifecycle.
